summary: Route (b) of the FS-GG/.github#4778 decision selects one fresh GitHub-hosted public-repo ubuntu-24.04 VM per BAR image operation. The cited no-content probe ran once (run 39944268141, image 20261012.334.1, 2026-10-23). It measured: one 150 GiB disk with no separate /mnt; / had 85.79 GiB free at baseline and 125.08 GiB after deleting about 42.6 GB of toolchains in 138 s; a single preallocated volume had 116.64 GiB free; MemAvailable was 14.59 GiB after stopping docker/containerd; nproc and affinity were 4; systemd-run Delegate=yes worked for root and the runner user; /dev/kvm worked after a udev rule. The host has Buildah 1.33.7 and lacks the controller's Arch library pins. Buildah 1.43.1 and all 13 pins came only from a digest-pinned Arch userland with archived packages. So #1032's 80 GiB, 14 GiB and 4-CPU floors were met on that VM. This is not a guarantee: GitHub documents 14 GB of disk, and the admission refusals stay authoritative. Caveats found: mkfs.ext4's default discard punched the fallocated loop backing sparse (use -E nodiscard and re-read allocated blocks); the Arch userland must not need docker, which is stopped at admission; Ubuntu sets apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1. The memory margin was about 605 MiB and the CPU margin zero. The probe is not image evidence and admits no BAR operation.
title: Hosted-VM BAR resource domain measured feasible; preallocation and daemon caveats
